{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p="specs/001-transactions/research.md"
s=open(p).read()
new_items="""## R8. invalidate_many any/all semantics (R04)

- **Decision**: `invalidate_many(tags, mode='any')` validates `mode` in
  `{"any", "all"}` and validates `tags` with the exact same rules as
  `put` (bare string rejected, finite iterable of str, dedup via
  frozenset, generators consumed once). Matching: `any` -> keys in the
  union of `_tag_keys[t]` over requested tags; `all` -> intersection
  (keys present in every requested tag's set, computed as
  `set.intersection(*sets)` over non-empty sets). Empty requested tag
  set -> returns 0 and removes nothing in BOTH modes (explicitly
  supersedes the old design note "empty all-tags matches every key").
  Returns the number of distinct removed keys. Removal reuses the same
  `_remove(key)` choke point as `invalidate`.
- **Rationale**: Union/intersection over the existing `tag -> set[key]`
  index gives O(sum of tag set sizes) matching with O(removed) mutation;
  reusing `_remove` guarantees invariant 3 (no stale memberships).
  `invalidate(tag)` is implemented as `invalidate_many((tag,), 'any')`
  semantics (identical result), keeping one code path.
- **Alternatives considered**:
  1. Scan all live keys and test tag sets per key - rejected: O(n)
     per call vs O(matched) with the index.
  2. `all` mode with empty set matches every key (old design note) -
     REJECTED per R04: empty removes zero in either mode; the old prose
     is superseded and SC-006 requires a test proving it.

## R9. resize mechanics (R05)

- **Decision**: `resize(maxsize)` validates capacity with the R4 rule
  FIRST. On success: if shrinking, evict via repeated
  `self._cache.popitem()` (public LRU method) routed through
  `_remove(key)` until `len(self._cache) <= maxsize`; then update the
  internal capacity attribute (`self._cache._LRUCache__maxsize` - the
  name-mangled backing field of the `maxsize` property, only write
  target that avoids rebuilding). Growing: update the capacity
  attribute only; no eviction. On failure: `ValueError`, zero state
  change. The `maxsize` property on TaggedCache delegates to
  `self._cache.maxsize`, so it reports the current capacity after
  resize.
- **Rationale**: `popitem()` evicts in true LRU order (the only
  observable recency order - `__iter__` is insertion order, observed).
  Updating the backing attribute preserves every surviving entry object
  and its recency position exactly (R05 + round-2 clarification: no
  re-copying, no recomputation of any per-entry state). Rebuilding a
  new LRUCache would re-insert keys in iteration (insertion) order,
  silently corrupting recency - rejected.
- **Alternatives considered**:
  1. Rebuild `self._cache = LRUCache(new_maxsize)` and re-put
     survivors - rejected: breaks LRU order (iteration is insertion
     order) and re-copies values.
  2. Expose a `maxsize.setter` on `Cache`/`LRUCache` - rejected: would
     modify existing upstream files (Constitution Principle I).
- **Risk note (Principle V)**: writing the name-mangled attribute is
  the one coupling point to LRUCache internals; it is confined to
  `tagged.py`, guarded by a single helper, and covered by a
  shrink/grow/failed-resize test asserting full state preservation
  (order verified via subsequent eviction order).

## R10. Generator tags and detachment (R06)

- **Decision**: Tag validation iterates the supplied iterable exactly
  once (`list(iter(tags))` after the bare-string guard) - a generator is
  consumed once and never re-iterated; on any validation failure nothing
  is stored and the cache is unchanged. Detachment: `deepcopy` on input
  and output (R6 decision) already guarantees returned values stay
  detached across repeated gets and puts, including nested
  lists/dicts; the milestone-2 requirement adds no new mechanism, only
  explicit tests (mutate a returned nested list, re-get, assert
  isolation; repeat after puts).
- **Rationale**: One consumption pass is the only reading of "consumed
  only once" and the only one that is safe for one-shot generators;
  `deepcopy` is the established detachment mechanism (R6).
- **Alternatives considered**: accept an already-materialized list only -
  rejected: spec explicitly allows generators.

## Open items

None remaining. R5 and R9 carry risk notes that are tracked test
requirements (explicit tests), not unresolved questions. The Claim-A
round-2 expiry clarification (R07/R08) is recorded in spec.md
Assumptions: no expiry attribute exists in the frozen requirement set,
so resize preserves entry state as-is; revisit if a TTL milestone lands.
"""
anchor="## Open items

None remaining. R5's risk note is a tracked test requirement, not an
unresolved question."
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor,new_items,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
print("research.md lines:", s.count(chr(10)))
PYEOF"}
